scope: conditional configuration comparison; not runtime attestation or whole-service verification
shared_assumptions: The host, broker credential store and issuer keys are trusted and inaccessible to the guest.
Actual I/O refines the reviewed authorization/disclosure model; complete native refinement is still open.
Cryptographic primitives and authenticated transport meet their stated contracts.
The selected provider and reviewed release policy do not disclose credentials through unmodeled encodings or channels.

claim_labels.surrogate_binding: A stolen surrogate alone is insufficient
claim_labels.guest_file_key_theft_resistance: Guest files alone cannot copy the identity key

profiles.label: Local broker
profiles.setup: Host-local socket, capability and reviewed operation policy
profiles.availability: Python standalone workflow tested; no CA or TPM required. The native Rust acceptance workflow uses certificate binding.
profiles.limits: Local capabilities rely on socket/session isolation. No enrolled-key or hardware provenance claim.

profiles.label: Bound software key
profiles.setup: Add a CA, enrolled client certificate and certificate-bound surrogate
profiles.availability: Python and native Rust mTLS/provider workflows tested without TPM hardware.
profiles.limits: A copy of the client key plus certificate and surrogate can authenticate. Scope and revocation still apply.

profiles.label: Add a vTPM device
profiles.setup: Add swtpm and a VM device; keep the existing software identity key
profiles.availability: AIVM creation/offline upgrade has simulated-daemon coverage; real libvirt lifecycle validation is open.
profiles.limits: Device presence changes no key-custody claim. AIVM does not automatically move existing keys into a TPM.

profiles.label: Verified TPM key
profiles.setup: Generate/use a TPM key, independently establish its provenance, and enforce the enrollment assurance mode
profiles.availability: Native Rust has explicit TPM tooling/enrollment and isolated emulator tests. AIVM guest enrollment integration and real hardware provenance remain separate gates; Python parity is not claimed.
profiles.limits: Requires verified non-exportability, protected authorization and trusted TPM/AK provenance. Guest signing access can relay authentication. A vTPM host can copy its state.

profiles.label: Credential-bearing host program
profiles.setup: Keep the verified TPM client identity, but give an arbitrary host executable the provider credential
profiles.availability: Architecture comparison only; this work adds no host-exec feature.
profiles.limits: Even with strong client identity custody, an executable given a provider credential can disclose it. These are independent security dimensions.

never_inferred: That the host cannot copy software vTPM state
That an authorized guest cannot act as a signing relay
That the guest or a particular agent process is uncompromised
That a guest vTPM provides host rollback resistance
That a successful Lean model check proves complete deployed-service secrecy
